hints: Write line equation $y = mx - 2$ and equate to curve $x^2 - 2x + 7 = mx - 2$.
walkthrough:
Write the equation of the line passing through $(0, -2)$ with gradient $m$:
$$y = mx - 2$$

Equate the line and curve equations to find points of intersection:
$$x^2 - 2x + 7 = mx - 2 \implies x^2 - (2 + m)x + 9 = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition requiring discriminant $\Delta = 0$:
$$[-(2 + m)]^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0 \implies (2 + m)^2 = 36$$
$$2 + m = \pm 6 \implies m = 4 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -8$$

Find the point of contact for each value of $m$:
$$\text{For } m = 4: \quad x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0 \implies (x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = 3, \; y = 4(3) - 2 = 10 \implies (3, 10)$$
$$\text{For } m = -8: \quad x^2 + 6x + 9 = 0 \implies (x + 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = -3, \; y = -8(-3) - 2 = 22 \implies (-3, 22)$$
